speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome to Sorcery.
zh: 欢迎来到 Sorcery。

speaker: Unknown
en: The potential of photonics.
zh: 光子学的潜力。

speaker: Unknown
en: The technology to interconnect these GPUs.
zh: 互连这些 GPU 的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Global payroll and HR platform.
zh: 全球薪资和人力资源平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: 8 billion operational data points.
zh: 80 亿个运营数据点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Scale ups over startups.
zh: 规模化成长公司胜过初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'd rather have a million of something than one of anything.
zh: 你宁愿拥有一百万个某样东西,也不愿只有任何一个的一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Building the intelligence layer for defense.
zh: 为国防打造智能层。

speaker: Unknown
en: There isn't enough power.
zh: 电力不够了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's not enough memory chips.
zh: 内存芯片不够了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're at the end of physics of what we can still do.
zh: 我们已经到了物理极限,能做的都做完了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yannick and Herwig, welcome to Sorcery and Strikes Annual Gala.
zh: Yannick 和 Herwig,欢迎来到 Sorcery and Strikes 年度盛典。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're here in Monaco and we're going to go deep into photonics and what you're building with FEMA.
zh: 我们现在在摩纳哥,我们将深入探讨光子学以及你们用 FEMA 在构建的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But before we get into that, we're going to go into a long conversation on photonics.
zh: 但在进入那个话题之前,我们要先进行一场关于光子学的长谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Yannick, I'd love to start with your background and then Herwig, we'll get into yours.
zh: Yannick,我想从你的背景开始,然后我们再聊 Herwig 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you get into photonics?
zh: 你是怎么进入光子学领域的?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was one of these nerdy kids who locked himself up in his bedroom playing Lego all day.
zh: 我曾是那种整天把自己关在卧室里玩乐高的书呆子小孩。

speaker: Unknown
en: So naturally I went to engineering school and that was 20 years ago.
zh: 所以我自然而然地去了工程学院,那是 20 年前的事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And back then, Silicon Photonics was this niche upcoming branch in engineering.
zh: 那时候,硅光子学还只是工程学里一个冷门的、正在兴起的小分支,

speaker: Unknown
en: with no prospect for any job at all, so I decided to jump on that ship.
zh: 完全没有任何就业前景,所以我决定跳上那条船。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did my PhD in that field and then by that time I had the opportunity to move to San Diego to join a startup company there that was trying to commercialize silicon photonics, one of the first companies to do that.
zh: 我在那个领域读了博士,之后那段时间我有机会搬到圣地亚哥,加入那里的一家初创公司,那家公司试图将硅光子学商业化,是最早做这件事的公司之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to successfully do that, I moved back to iMac, where I worked on laser integration for silicon photonics for a while.
zh: 而为了成功做到这一点,我搬回了 iMac,在那里做了一段时间硅光子学的激光集成工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then five years ago, I joined NVIDIA, back then when I still had to explain to people what NVIDIA actually was.
zh: 然后五年前,我加入了 NVIDIA,那时候我还得向人们解释 NVIDIA 到底是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we started from scratch, built the silicon photonics technology there into a product-ready maturity.
zh: 于是我们从零开始,把那里的硅光子学技术打造到可产品化的成熟度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now I'm starting at TEMA.
zh: 现在我要加入 TEMA 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rorik, how did you get involved?
zh: Rorik,你是怎么参与进来的?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've been investor most of my life, turned operator very late, but I've been focused on deep tech for quite a while and so got involved in the fascinating world of photonics almost a decade ago and realized three, four years ago that the train was leaving the station and there were some gaping holes in the supply chain.
zh: 我大半辈子都是投资人,很晚才转为运营者,但我专注于深科技已经有相当长的时间了,所以差不多十年前就进入了光子学这个迷人的世界,并在三四年前意识到火车要离站了,而供应链中存在一些巨大的缺口。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is what we're trying to solve with Thema, realizing that, you know, this visionary choice of Yannick 20 years ago to study the field of silicon photonics was something that has put Belgium on the map and has created a talent base that's broad and deep.
zh: 这就是我们要用 Thema 解决的问题,要认识到,Yannick 20 年前选择研究硅光子学这个有远见的决定,把比利时推上了地图,并造就了一个既广又深的人才基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've spent my life selecting, honing and nurturing talent.
zh: 而我这一生都在挑选、磨练和培养人才。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's what we're going to hope and do with this.
zh: 所以这就是我们希望通过这件事去做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's lay out the state of the market and how chips have gotten to this point, why copper is going out of date and why there's a focus on photonics and lasers.
zh: 那么让我们来梳理一下市场现状,芯片是如何走到今天这一步的,为什么铜正在过时,以及为什么焦点在光子学和激光上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you explain a little bit of that and also why Europe?
zh: 你能解释一下这方面的情况,还有为什么是欧洲?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think the market is the part that really dragged me into it.
zh: 我认为市场正是真正把我拉进来的那部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: We saw a much bigger opportunity than what most people in the field were seeing.
zh: 我们看到的机会比这个领域大多数人看到的要大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was because we were talking to the CTOs of data centers and realized indeed what their need was and how photonics could help.
zh: 那是因为我们和数据中心的首席技术官们交谈,真正了解到了他们的需求以及光子学能如何提供帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were listening very carefully when some of the gurus of the ecosystem, like Andy Bechtelsheim, were quoting numbers that far exceeded what even the most optimistic analysts were saying.
zh: 当生态系统中的一些大师级人物,比如 Andy Bechtelsheim,引用那些甚至超过了最乐观分析师所说的数字时,我们也在非常仔细地倾听。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we felt that they were, you know, very well informed.
zh: 我们觉得他们,你知道,消息非常灵通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's what pushed us to do this.
zh: 所以这就是推动我们做这件事的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to answer your question about where we are today, so if you think about AI, you think about GPUs, right?
zh: 至于回答你关于我们今天所处位置的问题——想想 AI,你就会想到 GPU,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You think about these compute engines that actually run the models, but the models have gotten so large that they no longer fit on a single GPU.
zh: 你会想到这些真正运行模型的计算引擎,但这些模型已经大到无法装进单个 GPU 里了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we need to do is we need to interconnect multiple GPUs together to run these models.
zh: 所以我们需要做的是把多个 GPU 互连起来一起运行这些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Traditionally, that's been copper interconnects, but as these GPUs get faster, they need more data, they need more data at a faster rate, and copper is running out of steam.
zh: 传统上用的是铜互连,但随着这些 GPU 变得越来越快,它们需要更多数据,需要以更快的速度获取更多数据,而铜已经力不从心了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why we're transitioning to optical interconnects, which bring much higher data transfer bandwidths.
zh: 这就是为什么我们正在转向光互连,它能带来高得多的数据传输带宽。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, that's where...
zh: 所以,是的,这就是……

speaker: Unknown
en: So I recently interviewed Tony Kim of BlackRock in Paris at the Raise AI Summit.
zh: 我最近在巴黎的 Raise AI 峰会上采访了 BlackRock 的 Tony Kim。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were breaking down the entire industry.
zh: 我们把整个行业拆解了一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says there's a $10 trillion rebuild that's happening.
zh: 他说正在发生一场 10 万亿美元的重建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the most affected and going to be the most effective places for that spend is in these data centers because the current old infrastructure of a data center is not built for AI.
zh: 而受影响最大、也将是这笔支出最有效落点的地方之一就是这些数据中心,因为数据中心现有的老旧基础设施不是为 AI 而建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's completely inefficient.
zh: 它完全低效。

speaker: Unknown
en: It takes a lot of water, it takes a lot of energy, and the chips that are being used in those are just they're just all outdated and they cannot handle the parameter models that are in the market.
zh: 它消耗大量的水、大量的能源,而且其中使用的芯片全都过时了,无法应对市面上的参数模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would love to get kind of an understanding from one of you the difference in architecture of those data centers and how they're transforming with this new build.
zh: 所以我很想从你们中的一位那里了解一下，这些数据中心的架构有什么不同，以及随着这种新建设它们正在如何转型。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's probably for you.
zh: 这可能是问你的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you compare a traditional hyperscale data center to a modern AI factory, one of the big differences is that there is way more traffic between different servers.
zh: 如果你比较传统超大规模数据中心和现代 AI 工厂，其中一个很大的区别是，不同服务器之间的流量要多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about your traditional Google search five years ago, it was basically your traffic is routed to one computer that
zh: 如果你想想五年前传统的 Google 搜索，基本上是你的流量被路由到一台计算机，

speaker: Unknown
en: Finds the answer and sends that answer back.
zh: 找到答案并把那个答案发回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, if you think about modern AI infrastructure, there's, as I said before, the models no longer fit on a single GPU.
zh: 现在，如果你想想现代 AI 基础设施，正如我之前所说，模型不再能装进单个 GPU 里了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's already GPU to GPU communication, but now in the age of agentic AI, there's a model that is doing a call to some tool, which is on a different server that's returning the results to the GPU.
zh: 所以已经有 GPU 到 GPU 的通信，而现在在智能体 AI 的时代，有一个模型要调用某个工具，这个工具在另一台服务器上，并把结果返回给 GPU。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a lot of traffic within
zh: 所以数据中心内部有大量的流量，

speaker: Unknown
en: The data center, which is very sensitive to latency, basically the time between when all these different calculations can run.
zh: 这些流量对延迟非常敏感，基本上就是所有这些不同计算之间运行所需的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what that means in reality is that you need a much flatter network instead of a really deep hierarchical tree of switches.
zh: 所以这在现实中意味着，你需要一个平坦得多的网络，而不是一个非常深的层次化交换机树。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need a much flatter network that means far more connections between direct connections between switches and GPU.
zh: 你需要一个平坦得多的网络，这意味着交换机与 GPU 之间要有多得多的直连。

speaker: Unknown
en: So basically a much denser network than what we had in the traditional hyperscale.
zh: 所以基本上是一个比传统超大规模时代密集得多的网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're asking a CTO of a data center what keeps you awake at night, the energy consumption is answer number one because it's existential to them.
zh: 如果你问一个数据中心的 CTO 是什么让他夜不能寐，能耗是第一位的答案，因为这对他们来说是生死攸关的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't know how to solve it.
zh: 他们不知道怎么解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their CEO is saying, we need to grow, we need to grow.
zh: 他们的 CEO 在说，我们要增长，我们要增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's saying, okay, but where?
zh: 而他在说，好吧，但在哪儿增长？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because nobody can deliver the grid.
zh: 因为没有人能交付电网。

speaker: Unknown
en: Google negotiated for three years with Amsterdam and had to move its plans to actually now Belgium because they simply can't get the grid.
zh: Google 与阿姆斯特丹谈判了三年，最后不得不把计划转移到现在的比利时，因为他们就是拿不到电网。

speaker: Unknown
en: That obviously with the ambitious growth plans that they have requires a much more fundamental solution that can scale to the same size as the problem, right?
zh: 显然，凭他们雄心勃勃的增长计划，这需要一个能扩展到与问题同等规模的更根本的解决方案，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there are many data centers, there are many more being planned.
zh: 所以现在有很多数据中心，还有更多在规划中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Therefore, you know, upgrading the grid or building new power plants cannot happen in the time that is required.
zh: 因此，你知道的，升级电网或建造新电厂无法在所需的时间内完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where, you know,
zh: 而这就是，

speaker: Unknown
en: Every deep deck paradigm shift needs a killer app for photonics more than 20 years in the making, 30 years in the making on the science side.
zh: 每一个深科技范式转变都需要一个光子学的杀手级应用，这是在科学方面酝酿了 20 多年、30 多年的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Energy consumption by data centers and AI is that killer app.
zh: 数据中心和 AI 的能耗就是那个杀手级应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now we get to where we are today, which is...
zh: 所以现在我们到了今天所处的位置，那就是……

speaker: Unknown
en: That's great, but nobody was prepared for the speed of change.
zh: 那很好，但没有人对变化的速度做好准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: The speed of change happened November 22, ChatGPT comes out.
zh: 变化的速度发生在 2022 年 11 月，ChatGPT 发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: It goes viral like it never seen before.
zh: 它以前所未见的方式病毒式传播。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with the growth of that came this requirement or this realization, okay, we need to switch to photonics.
zh: 随着它的增长，带来了这个需求或者说这个认识：好吧，我们需要转向光子学。

speaker: Unknown
en: NVIDIA took the lead in that.
zh: NVIDIA 在这方面领先。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were, I mean, they had been talking about photonics for a long time, but they said, okay, we need to make the switch happen.
zh: 我是说，他们谈论光子学已经很久了，但他们说，好吧，我们需要让这个转变发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: 24, they were even louder about it.
zh: 24 年，他们的声音更大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: 25, they really pushed the market, and 26.
zh: 25 年，他们真正推动了市场，然后 26 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: They showed the market what they meant with their investments in Lumentum, Coherent.
zh: 他们用对 Lumentum、Coherent 的投资向市场展示了他们的意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've invested 4x, the total market size, in the first six months of this year.
zh: 他们在今年头六个月里投资了整个市场规模的四倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now everybody realizes, oh, the supply chain is not ready.
zh: 所以现在每个人都意识到，哦，供应链还没准备好。

speaker: Unknown
en: The innovation is ready.
zh: 创新是准备好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The photonic scientists have done a lot of work.
zh: 光子学科学家已经做了大量工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: The photonic designers have done a lot of work.
zh: 光子学设计师已经做了大量工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you need to work that all the way back to the beginning, which is, you know, all the way from the raw material over the tooling, over the infrastructure to build.
zh: 但你需要把这些一直追溯到最源头，也就是，你知道的，从原材料到工装，到用于建设的基础设施，整条链路。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's where the pain point sits today.
zh: 而我认为这就是今天痛点所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's part of what we are trying to solve.
zh: 这也是我们正在试图解决的问题的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how many photonic companies are out there?
zh: 那么市面上有多少家光子学公司呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: I interviewed the Lumentum CEO, Michael Hurston.
zh: 我采访了 Lumentum 的 CEO Michael Hurston。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even just looking at that company, they are spilling over with demand.
zh: 仅看那一家公司，他们的需求已经满溢出来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their stock went up 1,000 times in a year.
zh: 他们的股票一年涨了一千倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Insane.
zh: 疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he had just stepped in maybe a year and a half ago.
zh: 而他大概是一年半前才刚加入的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he really came in at an opportune time.
zh: 所以他真的是在恰好的时机进来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'm curious, what does the state of the market look like for the companies that are existing?
zh: 但我很好奇，对于现有的这些公司来说，市场的现状是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how does it all work together?
zh: 这一切又是如何协同运作的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, again, what needs to be understood is the shift in size of the market.
zh: 我认为，再次强调，需要理解的是市场规模的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Photonics for years was an academic endeavor with some applications that was being prepared for in the supply chain at that scale.
zh: 光子学多年来一直是一项学术事业，只有一些应用，供应链当时是在为那个规模做准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now, all of a sudden, NVIDIA steps in and says, no, no, guys, this is much, much bigger.
zh: 而现在，突然间，NVIDIA 进场说，不不，伙计们，这要大得多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, obviously, Lamentum Coherent are the two leading companies in the West doing this.
zh: 所以，你知道，显然，Lamentum 和 Coherent 是西方做这件事的两家领先公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're the only ones scaled at that size.
zh: 他们是唯一有那种规模的玩家。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at the rest of the industry, the traditional players, the TSMCs, Global Foundries, Towers of this world have made a tremendous effort investing in the part that fits in their supply, in their production process, which is the front end, the silicon photonics, so making the wafers.
zh: 如果你看看行业的其他部分，那些传统玩家，这个世界的 TSMC、Global Foundries、Towers 们，已经在投资他们供应链中适合他们生产流程的那部分上付出了巨大努力，也就是前端，硅光子学，即制造晶圆。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you deliver a wafer to NVIDIA, that's not what they ordered.
zh: 但如果你把一片晶圆交付给 NVIDIA，那不是他们订购的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: They ordered a final chip.
zh: 他们订购的是最终芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a lot of other things required.
zh: 所以还需要很多其他东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lasers first and foremost, which is what Lumentum and others are making.
zh: 首先是激光器，这正是 Lumentum 和其他公司在制造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's going to have to scale by a lot.
zh: 而这部分将不得不大规模扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's challenging because
zh: 而这很有挑战性，因为

speaker: Unknown
en: The throughput of the machines is not at all where it needs to be.
zh: 机器的产能完全达不到它需要达到的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: The efficiency, the yield is not what it's supposed to be.
zh: 效率、良率也不是它应该有的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the substrates, the raw material is really, really cornered.
zh: 而衬底，即原材料，真的是非常被卡脖子。

speaker: Unknown
en: The market is, I mean, there's only a handful of suppliers.
zh: 这个市场，我是说，供应商只有寥寥几家。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on top of all these problems, you now have the East-West divide, which is getting quite problematic.
zh: 而在所有这些问题之上，你现在还有东西方分化，这正变得相当成问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in all of that, we think Europe is in a sweet spot.
zh: 所以在这一切之中，我们认为欧洲处于一个绝佳位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because in Europe, you have industrial capacity that was available, industrial infrastructure that was available, that's what we bought.
zh: 因为在欧洲，你有可用的工业产能、可用的工业基础设施，这就是我们买下的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have photonic talent that has been trained for decades.
zh: 你有已经受训几十年的光子学人才。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have industrial talent
zh: 你有工业人才

speaker: Unknown
en: That was available because all the big foundries closed.
zh: 之所以可用，是因为所有大型代工厂都关闭了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the combination of all of this in addition with a desire of European sovereignty makes that we're like in an ideal spot to do this from Europe.
zh: 所以这一切的结合，再加上欧洲主权自主的愿望，使得我们处于从欧洲做这件事的理想位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's go to the founding of the company and how you guys came together.
zh: 那么我们谈谈公司的创立，以及你们是如何走到一起的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was that process like?
zh: 那个过程是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have been building the concept of a pure play photonic foundry at a much larger scale.
zh: 我们一直在构建一个更大规模的纯粹光子代工厂的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were looking around.
zh: 我们当时在四处观察。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were seeing that all the big guys were doing the front end of the process, as I said, the silicon wafers.
zh: 我们看到所有大厂都在做流程的前端，正如我所说，硅晶圆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were seeing a lot of innovation happening, but that was mostly university spin-out scale.
zh: 我们也看到很多创新在发生，但那大多是大学衍生公司规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there wasn't really an industrial player in the middle.
zh: 所以中间并没有真正的工业玩家。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as we were making plans in 23, 24 to do this, there was, I guess, some serendipity involved in that a large scale European foundry went out of business.
zh: 而当我们在 23、24 年制定计划要做这件事时，我想，也有某种机缘巧合，一家大型欧洲代工厂歇业了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so
zh: 于是

speaker: Unknown
en: We took the occasion, we jumped on it, we bought it, and it delivered, I think, a very nice combination.
zh: 我们抓住这个机会，我们跳了上去，我们买下了它，我认为它带来了非常不错的组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, 20 kilometers away from IMAC, the world leading research center, lots of talent.
zh: 其一，距离 IMAC 这个世界领先的研究中心 20 公里，人才济济。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two, lots of industrial talent, as I said, and infrastructure that was ready to go right at the time when everybody needs it, because when you want to build a foundry of this size, you're talking about a three to five year project.
zh: 其二，如我所说，大量工业人才，以及正好在所有人都需要它的时刻随时可用的基础设施，因为当你想建造这种规模的代工厂，你说的是一个三到五年的项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's between getting the permits and the licenses and building that whole, it's not just clean rooms, the infrastructure is quite complex.
zh: 从拿到许可证和执照，到建起整个设施，这不只是洁净室，基础设施相当复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: So having all of it ready to go in 24 was, you know, a serendipitous event, I'll call it that.
zh: 所以在 24 年就拥有一切随时可用的东西，你知道，我会把这称为机缘巧合的事件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's where we jumped on it.
zh: 所以我们就跳上去抓住了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we started talking to both sides at the same time.
zh: 然后我们开始同时与双方对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I say both sides, we started talking to the industrial talent and the photonic talent and said, look,
zh: 我说双方，是指我们开始与工业人才和光子学人才对话，并说，听着，

speaker: Unknown
en: Europe has invested, successfully invested, for 20, 30 years in photonic innovation.
zh: 欧洲在光子学创新上已经成功投资了 20、30 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the time for industrialization.
zh: 现在是工业化的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, Yannick and others jumped on board instantly.
zh: 然后，你知道，Yannick 和其他人立刻加入了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's where we are.
zh: 所以这就是我们的现状。

speaker: Unknown
en: This episode is brought to you by Brex, my favorite.
zh: 本集节目由 Brex 呈现，我的最爱。

speaker: Unknown
en: You become what you spend on, and I refuse to spend my time on work that shouldn't exist.
zh: 你会变成你花钱的方向，而我拒绝把时间花在不应该存在的工作上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Expense reports, receipt chasing, and manual closes.
zh: 报销单、追发票，以及手动结账。

speaker: Unknown
en: The companies building what's next from Vercel, OpenAI, Anthropic, Granola, and Deepgram all made the same call.
zh: 那些正在构建未来的公司——Vercel、OpenAI、Anthropic、Granola 和 Deepgram——都做出了同样的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all run on Brex.
zh: 它们都运行在 Brex 上。

en: Brex is the intelligent finance platform that combines cards, expenses, and banking into a single stack,
zh: Brex 是智能金融平台,将卡、报销和银行业务整合到一个统一的技术栈中,

speaker: Unknown
en: With agentic finance built in.
zh: 内置智能体金融功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI agents that handle expenses automatically, enforce policy before spend happens, and close your books in minutes.
zh: AI 智能体自动处理报销,在支出发生前执行政策,并在几分钟内完成结账。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why Sorcery runs on Brex, so I can spend time on building and not busy work.
zh: 这就是 Sorcery 运行在 Brex 上的原因,这样我就可以把时间花在构建上,而不是繁琐的事务上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's time to get Brex AF.
zh: 是时候 Get Brex AF 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more at brex.com slash sorcery.
zh: 访问 brex.com/sorcery 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's B-R-E-X dot com slash S-O-U-R-C-E-R-Y.
zh: 那是 B-R-E-X 点 com 斜杠 S-O-U-R-C-E-R-Y。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bye.
zh: 再见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Turing is training the next generation of AI with tasks that require real expertise and real-world judgment.
zh: Turing 正在用需要真正专业知识和现实世界判断力的任务来训练下一代 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why companies like NVIDIA, Anthropic, Salesforce, and Gemini partner with Turing.
zh: 这就是为什么 NVIDIA、Anthropic、Salesforce 和 Gemini 这样的公司与 Turing 合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Turing builds realistic reinforcement learning environments and data systems based on real operational traces, the kind of infrastructure Frontier Labs need to train superintelligence.
zh: Turing 基于真实运营轨迹构建逼真的强化学习环境和数据系统,这正是前沿实验室训练超级智能所需的那类基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit Turing.com slash S-O-U-R-C-E-R-Y.
zh: 访问 Turing.com/S-O-U-R-C-E-R-Y。

speaker: Unknown
en: Janik, from a technical standpoint, where are you at?
zh: Janik,从技术角度来说,你们现在进展到哪了?

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, I was in a great spot at NVIDIA, right?
zh: 是的,我当时在 NVIDIA 处于一个很好的位置,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: We were building the next generation of chips and I wasn't planning to go anywhere.
zh: 我们在构建下一代芯片,我本来不打算去任何地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when I started to talk to Herrick and I learned about the ambition of this enterprise and what he was planning to do, I realized that this was
zh: 但当我开始和 Herrick 交谈,了解到这家企业的雄心和他计划要做的事情时,我意识到这是一个

speaker: Unknown
en: a once in a lifetime opportunity for me to join a mission that's gonna solve some of the core problems that are slowing down probably one of the biggest or the biggest technological revolution that I will witness in my lifetime.
zh: 千载难逢的机会,让我能够加入一项使命,去解决一些正在拖慢——很可能是最大、或者就是最大的——我此生将见证的技术革命的核心问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I decided to leave the Golden Palace and jump onto the pirate ship and set sail.
zh: 所以我决定离开黄金宫殿,跳上海盗船,扬帆起航。

speaker: Unknown
en: Selfish question.
zh: 一个自私的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it like at NVIDIA?
zh: 在 NVIDIA 是什么样的体验?

speaker: Unknown
en: What have you learned there?
zh: 你在那里学到了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like operating principles?
zh: 比如运营原则?

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it actually like?
zh: 实际上是什么样子?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an incredible company.
zh: 它是一家了不起的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like a startup.
zh: 它感觉像一家初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very agile.
zh: 它非常敏捷。

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea is to fail fast.
zh: 理念就是快速失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we start building stuff.
zh: 所以我们开始构建东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it doesn't work, move to something new.
zh: 如果不奏效,就转向新的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's, in my experience, a very apolitical company.
zh: 以我的经验来看,它是一家非常没有政治内耗的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: The org chart is just a piece of paper.
zh: 组织架构图只是一张纸。

speaker: Unknown
en: If there's a project and you can contribute, you contribute to that project.
zh: 如果有一个项目而你能做出贡献,你就为那个项目做贡献。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't matter where you are in the org chart.
zh: 你在组织架构图上处于什么位置并不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, it's an incredible company.
zh: 所以是的,它是一家了不起的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then for people who don't know what iMac is, can you also explain iMac and where it fits in the stack?
zh: 那么对于不了解 iMac 的听众,你能否也解释一下 iMac 以及它在技术栈中所处的位置?

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: So iMac is a... And it's not iMac, by the way.
zh: iMac 是一个……顺便说一下,它不是 iMac。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not.
zh: 它不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I-M-E-C.
zh: 是 I-M-E-C。

speaker: Unknown
en: Inter-Universitary Microelectronics Center.
zh: Inter-Universitary Microelectronics Center(校际微电子中心)。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Microelectronics Center, that tells you something about how old this institution is.
zh: 微电子中心,这个名字能告诉你这个机构有多古老。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it started over 30 years ago and has been doing, has been spearheading research initially in the area of electronics, but since sometime also much broader area, one of these is photonics.
zh: 它成立于 30 多年前,一直在做、一直引领着最初在电子领域的研究,但从某个时候起也扩展到了更广泛的领域,其中之一就是光子学。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they started, they were
zh: 所以他们开始了,他们是

speaker: Unknown
en: IMEC was one of the birthplaces of silicon photonics in the world and has grown to be the number one research center when it comes to advanced electronics technologies in the world.
zh: IMEC 是世界上硅光子学的发源地之一,并且已经成长为世界上先进电子技术领域的头号研究中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And where are you guys at in terms of commercial progress to date?
zh: 那你们目前在商业化进展上处于什么阶段?

speaker: Unknown
en: When are you going to start rolling out your customers?
zh: 你们什么时候开始向客户推广?

speaker: Unknown
en: Our biggest challenge is the timeline customers are putting in front of us.
zh: 我们最大的挑战是客户摆在我们面前的时间表。

speaker: Unknown
en: The good news is that the volumes they're asking for even surpass our wildly ambitious projections.
zh: 好消息是,他们要求的数量甚至超过我们极其雄心勃勃的预测。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's certainly very positive.
zh: 所以这肯定是非常积极的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The constraints for us now, the whole market, Coherent, Lumentum and others, everybody is facing the same constraints.
zh: 我们现在面临的约束，整个市场，Coherent、Lumentum 以及其他公司，所有人都面临着同样的约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: The tool builders are not building anywhere near enough tools and the tools themselves need to be further improved for throughput, for efficiency, for yield.
zh: 工具制造商们建造的工具远远不够，而且这些工具本身在吞吐量、效率和良率方面还需要进一步改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then even more problematic, the substrates, so the raw material.
zh: 然后问题更大的是衬底，也就是原材料。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so here's the good news.
zh: 所以这里有个好消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: As I said, Europe has been investing successfully in innovation.
zh: 正如我所说，欧洲一直在成功地投资创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so some of these problems, even though they didn't anticipate this shift,
zh: 所以其中一些问题，尽管他们没有预料到这个转变，

speaker: Unknown
en: were being researched.
zh: 但一直在被研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so throughout Europe, Greece, Germany, Spain, France, Switzerland for sure, there has been a pipeline being built on tackling individual technical challenges around this.
zh: 所以在整个欧洲，希腊、德国、西班牙、法国，瑞士当然也算，一直有一条管线在建立，围绕这个方向攻克一个个技术难题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to answer your question, our timeline is to start producing next year in 27 and work towards a full ramp up by 28.
zh: 所以回答你的问题，我们的时间表是明年，也就是 27 年开始生产，并在 28 年前实现全面爬坡。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our timelines are short, but Europe is...
zh: 所以我们的时间表很短，但欧洲……

speaker: Unknown
en: It's wide awake and ready to go.
zh: 它已经完全清醒并蓄势待发。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not just a slogan.
zh: 这不只是一句口号。

speaker: Unknown
en: We feel it every day.
zh: 我们每天都能感受到。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a lot of collaboration going on.
zh: 所以现在有大量的合作在进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're finally starting to really work cross borders.
zh: 我们终于开始真正地跨境协作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm very optimistic about Europe playing a significant role and Thema playing a significant role in this.
zh: 我对欧洲在其中发挥重要作用、Thema 发挥重要作用非常乐观。

speaker: Unknown
en: Has it been hard to hire?
zh: 招人难吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That was the question I got most before I started because I was all alone.
zh: 这是我刚起步前被问得最多的问题，因为当时我孤身一人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody said, where are you going to find the talent?
zh: 所有人都说，你去哪里找人才？

speaker: Unknown
en: We are really enthusiastic about the people that are joining us.
zh: 我们对加入我们的人非常热情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's true for the board where we have three of the most senior people of iMac joined our board.
zh: 董事会也是如此，我们有 iMac 的三位最高资历的人加入了我们的董事会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, people like Yannick from NVIDIA, but we have people from AWS, we have people from TSMC, Lime Research, like the top companies.
zh: 显然，有像 NVIDIA 的 Yannick 这样的人，但我们还有来自 AWS 的人、来自 TSMC 的人、来自 Lime Research 的人，都是顶尖公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of talent.
zh: 人才很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many of them are European because...
zh: 他们中许多是欧洲人，因为……

speaker: Unknown
en: What Janik didn't say is that he chose a niche field to go and study in, but then you have the choice.
zh: Janik 没说的是，他选择了一个细分领域去深造，但之后你就面临选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: You either go abroad to work, at least at the time, or you become a banker.
zh: 你要么出国工作，至少在当时是这样，要么去当银行家。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's either or.
zh: 所以就是二选一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we're hoping to build with Thema is, you know, homegrown magnet for talent.
zh: 而我们希望通过 Thema 打造的，你知道的，是一个本土的人才磁石。

speaker: Unknown
en: That becomes a self-sustaining ecosystem of innovation and industrial production.
zh: 让它成为一个自我延续的创新与工业生产生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the question to your answer is no.
zh: 所以对你问题的回答是否定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have been very fortunate with attracting talent.
zh: 我们在吸引人才方面一直非常幸运。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Europe's been waiting for this?
zh: 所以欧洲一直在等待这个？

speaker: Unknown
en: Europe's been waiting for this.
zh: 欧洲一直在等待这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you read the website of the European Council on the European Chip Act 2, they say that they really want to prioritize photonics.
zh: 如果你去看欧洲理事会关于《欧洲芯片法案 2》的网站，他们说你真的想优先发展光子学。

speaker: Unknown
en: Within Photonics, they want to really focus on industrialization, pure play.
zh: 在光子学领域内，他们想真正专注于工业化、纯代工。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's almost like reading a definition of Thema.
zh: 所以这几乎就像在读 Thema 的定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's, you know, it has to do with European sovereignty, but it's also got to do with Europe realizes that...
zh: 而且我认为，你知道，这和欧洲主权有关，但也和欧洲意识到……

speaker: Unknown
en: It has what it takes to not just play, but actually win in this game.
zh: 它具备的不只是参与这场游戏，而是真正赢得这场游戏的实力有关。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my favorite statistics from one of our board members who was the visionary professor who founded the photonics department at the University of Ghent, between 2000 and 2015, there were 4,000 peer-reviewed white papers on photonics globally.
zh: 我最喜欢的一个统计数据来自我们的一位董事会成员，他是创立根特大学光子学系的有远见的教授：2000 年到 2015 年间，全球有 4000 篇关于光子学的同行评审白皮书。

speaker: Unknown
en: 35% of them came from the University of Ghent.
zh: 其中 35% 来自根特大学。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think with the exception of Biscoff and chocolate, Belgium has no dominance like that in any other field.
zh: 我想除了华夫饼和巧克力之外，比利时在任何其他领域都没有这样的主导地位。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious for both of your answers for this question, but...
zh: 这个问题我想听听你们两位的回答，但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if you travel to America much, what your exposure is like, but I'm very curious for both of your answers for what do you think the biggest misconceptions are with European AI?
zh: 我不知道你们是否常去美国，接触多不多，但我很好奇你们两位的回答：你认为关于欧洲 AI 最大的误解是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I have to think about that.
zh: 我得想一想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Biggest misconceptions on European AI?
zh: 关于欧洲 AI 最大的误解？

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe I'll flip it around so I can tell you what...
zh: 也许我反过来讲，这样我可以告诉你……

speaker: Unknown
en: American Tier 1 potential customers asked us when they started speaking to us, which in and of itself was surprising.
zh: 美国的 Tier 1 潜在客户在开始和我们接触时问了我们什么，这本身就令人惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were a startup with two people at that point in time, so they shouldn't be talking to us, but they were.
zh: 我们当时是一家只有两个人的初创公司，所以他们本不该和我们谈的，但他们谈了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what did they challenge us with?
zh: 那他们向我们提出了什么挑战？

speaker: Unknown
en: What did they ask us?
zh: 他们问了我们什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: One is, you know, can you find the funding?
zh: 第一，你能不能找到资金？

speaker: Unknown
en: Two, can you find the talent?
zh: 第二，你能不能找到人才？

speaker: Unknown
en: Three, can you find the machines and the substrates and everything else?
zh: 第三，你能不能找到机器和基板以及其他所有东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: And within all of that, how on earth are you going to respect the timelines we require from you?
zh: 而在这一切之中，你到底要怎么遵守我们要求的时间表？

speaker: Unknown
en: So the conception of your... Heard about the summers here.
zh: 所以对你……的构想，听说过这里的夏天。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the conception of Europe is that it's slow, it's committee-driven decision-making.
zh: 对欧洲的刻板印象是它很慢，是委员会式的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what we're definitely incorporating in Thema is like what Yannick said.
zh: 所以我们在 Thema 里明确要融入的，就像 Yannick 说的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, this culture of fail fast, make decisions, drive forward, don't expect 100% perfect information.
zh: 你知道，这种快速失败、做决策、向前推进、不要指望 100% 完美信息的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: That may not be very European, but you know, the world is globalized.
zh: 这可能不太欧洲，但你知道，世界是全球化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're awake and we're going to adhere to, you know, we're going to take the best of the American culture as well in the firm.
zh: 我们醒着，而且我们要遵守，你知道，我们要把美国文化中最好的部分也带进这家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was in California last week.
zh: 我上周在加州。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I drove from San Francisco airport to Santa Clara, along the highway, there's all these billboards on AI stuff.
zh: 当我从旧金山机场开车去圣克拉拉时，沿着高速公路，到处都是关于 AI 的广告牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can feel there's incredible excitement about AI and the...
zh: 所以你能感觉到人们对 AI 有一种难以置信的兴奋，还有那……

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think many people like those billboards that live there.
zh: 我不觉得住在那里的很多人喜欢那些广告牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's another thing, but you can feel the excitement, right?
zh: 那是另一回事，但你能感觉到那种兴奋，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we have a very similar excitement here in Europe.
zh: 而且我认为我们在欧洲也有非常相似的兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: We may not be as vocal about it, but we're going to turn that excitement into a reality.
zh: 我们可能没那么大声地说出来，但我们要把那种兴奋变成现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there as much hate for data centers here as there is in America?
zh: 这里对数据中心的反感和美国一样多吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's a huge media propaganda thing, I'll be clear with that, in America, but I'm really curious how it's playing out here.
zh: 我是说，在美国那很大程度上是媒体的宣传攻势，这点我跟你说清楚，但我真的很好奇它在欧洲是如何上演的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Europe doesn't have the same, obviously, network of data centers than the US has.
zh: 欧洲显然没有像美国那样的数据中心网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: The regulations here are a lot stricter.
zh: 这里的法规严格得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I mean, I would almost flip it around.
zh: 所以，我是说，我几乎想把它反过来。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the opportunity for us, right?
zh: 那正是我们的机会，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: If we can help build the infrastructure that makes this whole business a lot more energy efficient.
zh: 如果我们能帮助建设基础设施，让整个行业的能效大幅提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then hopefully we will also start building out in Europe our own homegrown data center network, which may look very different than the mega hyperscalers that the US has built.
zh: 那么希望我们也能在欧洲开始建设我们自己本土的数据中心网络，它可能看起来和美国人建的那些超大规模数据中心非常不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's part of the problem that we're trying to solve.
zh: 但那正是我们试图解决的问题的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Europe doesn't have the same aversion towards it because it simply doesn't have the problem because it was regulated before the problem arose.
zh: 所以欧洲对它没有同样的反感，因为它根本不存在这个问题，因为在问题出现之前就已经被监管了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the timelines that you think upon?
zh: 你们考虑的是什么时间表？

speaker: Unknown
en: I ask this to people all the time.
zh: 我总是问人们这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I talk to aerospace companies.

speaker: Unknown
en: They're like, we're in dog years.

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a month is like 10 years for us.

speaker: Unknown
en: But then you have like other companies that are like a year.
zh: 但然后你也会遇到那种按年算的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: But anyways, what timeline do you think upon?
zh: 不管怎样，你们考虑的是什么时间表？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what are you most looking forward to within that timeline?
zh: 在那个时间表里，你们最期待的是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We're getting ready for production in 27.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我最期待的，确实是证明我们将要覆盖的从 LAP 到 FAP 之间的巨大空白。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have the right team on board to do that.
zh: 而且我们有合适的团队来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Still a lot of ground to be covered.
zh: 仍然有大量的路要走。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wouldn't call it low hanging fruits, but the experience of the team combined with the volcanic talent is going to allow us to beat expectations on that.
zh: 我不会称之为唾手可得的果实，但团队的经验加上 volcanic 的人才，将使我们能够超越预期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's what I'm looking forward to.
zh: 所以这就是我所期待的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The bar is high, but I think we can beat expectations.
zh: 门槛很高，但我认为我们能超越预期。

speaker: Unknown
en: Janik, what are you most looking forward to?
zh: Janik,你最期待的是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just getting started.
zh: 就是开始干起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: See how the community reacts, adjust to that and build some world-class manufacturing capability here in Europe.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: No.

speaker: Unknown
en: Unicorn.

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be like...

speaker: Unknown
en: I think both of these are true, actually.

speaker: Unknown
en: That's going to exist.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
